case_text: SYNTHETIC CASE (fictional). 41-year-old woman with a long history of migraine. Today, a sudden severe headache reached its peak within a minute while she was lifting a box. She calls it the worst headache of her life. Neck is stiff. She vomited twice. Neurological examination is normal. Her usual migraines build over an hour and have an aura. Takes no regular medicines.
evidence_topics: subarachnoid haemorrhage CT head lumbar puncture

must_catch.why: Her migraine history is a tempting anchor; this headache is different.

must_not_claim.why: A thunderclap headache is never managed by reassurance alone.
